result:
Task complete. Summary:

**Investigation first** (per the task's own instruction to check PR #596 before deciding where work belongs): PROJEXA holds no construction data of its own — everything lives in VERIDIAN (`compliance-tracker`). That repo's PR #596 had already built most of the revision-chain infrastructure (`parentBoqId`/`version` chain, `createBoqRevision`, `diffLineItems`/`compareBoq`, and a "warn if scope already executed" check against real work-progress data). So this task became closing four concrete, real gaps rather than rebuilding from scratch.

**compliance-tracker** (PR [#605](https://github.com/FChecklist/compliance-tracker/pull/605)):
- Upgraded the negative-variation warning into a real `409` hard block inside `createBoqRevision`'s transaction, with an explicit `allowScopeReductionOverride` escape hatch
- Generalized `compareBoq` to diff any two revisions, not just adjacent ones
- Added a computed `totalVariation` (running total variation value)
- Added the missing `/api/v1/projexa/scope/[id]/{revisions,compare}` routes PROJEXA needs
- 5 new pure unit tests, all passing; tsc clean; CI guardrail scripts pass

**projexa** (PR [#57](https://github.com/FChecklist/projexa/pull/57)):
- Proxy routes for the new endpoints
- Extended the existing Scope of Work screen with a variation column, New Revision dialog, and Compare dialog, surfacing the 409 block with an override action
- 6 new route tests + full existing suite passing, tsc clean

Both PRs are open, not merged — awaiting supervisor audit as instructed. PROGRESS.md in both repos documents the honest limitations (no separate Rev0/Rev1 label column; approval workflow not re-exposed).
